answer.text: Pension funds such as NPS (National Pension System)

explanation.text: The Logic: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), established under the PFRDA Act, 2013, regulates and develops the pension sector in India, including the National Pension System (NPS) and the Atal Pension Yojana (APY). It is distinct from SEBI (which regulates the securities market and mutual funds), RBI (banking) and IRDAI (insurance). The Trap: Option A (mutual funds) sits with SEBI. Option B (insurance) sits with IRDAI. Option C (bank deposits) sits with RBI. Although NPS invests across equity and debt similar to mutual funds, the NPS product is regulated by PFRDA, not SEBI. Note: The cited NISM Series V-B workbook focuses on mutual funds and does not, in the pages reviewed, contain a direct statement that 'PFRDA regulates NPS/APY'. The framing above reflects publicly known Indian financial-sector regulatory architecture rather than a direct workbook citation.
